scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for morpholine [2]. Morpholine is an organic amine compound primarily utilized in industrial settings as a volatile corrosion inhibitor in steam boiler systems, as well as an intermediate in the synthesis of rubber additives, pharmaceuticals, and agricultural chemicals.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Morpholine (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, all morpholine manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 12084 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally distributed in the domestic market. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial chemical compounds, as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Polyaluminium and organic chemical containers of morpholine conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).
The minimum allowed purity of the chemical must be 99.0 percent by mass, tested in accordance with the acidimetric titration method specified in Annex B.
The relative density of the liquid compound at 20/20 °C must be a minimum of 1.001, evaluated per Annex C.
The colour of morpholine must be clear and light, not exceeding 15 units on the Platinum-Cobalt (Pt-Co) scale when tested per IS 3025 (Part 4).
Boiling range characteristics must be highly controlled: the temperature must remain between 125 °C and 129 °C for 90 percent recovery of the distilled fraction when tested per IS 5298.
To prevent particulate fouling, residues on evaporation must not exceed a maximum of 1000 mg/l (Annex D), and the ash content must not exceed 0.003 g/100 ml (Annex E).
Trace contaminants must remain within low safety thresholds: Silica (as SiO2) is restricted to a maximum of 5 ppm, and Chloride (as Cl) is limited to a maximum of 5 ppm.
The maximum permissible concentration for trace iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and nickel (Ni) impurities is strictly limited to 5 ppm each.

requirements.requirement_type: Sample Preparation for Cu, Fe, and Ni by ICP (Annex F - Amended)
requirements.detail: In case of determination by ICP-OES or ICP-MS, sample preparation must be followed as per F-1. Reagents include de-ionized water, 96% H2SO4, 70% HClO4, 65% HNO3, 36% HCl, 99.9% Cs2SO4, and a mixed acid (HNO3:H2SO4:HClO4, 2:1:1 ratio) or Acid Mixture 1 (H2SO4:HNO3, 39:1 ratio with 2.2 g/l Cs2SO4). Weigh 0.35 g to 0.40 g of sample into the automated digestion system, add acid mixture, crack at 320 °C, completely digest organic remnants at 160 °C, evaporate to dryness, boil residue with 5% HCl, and perform duplicate determinations to report the mean value.

requirements.requirement_type: Sample Preparation for Silica by ICP (Annex F - Amended)
requirements.detail: In case of determination by ICP-OES or ICP-MS, sample preparation must be followed as per F-2. Reagents include 50% HCl, 0.4 g K2CO3-Na2CO3 and 0.1 g Na2B4O7 (soda-borax, 4:1 w/w mix). Pre-condition a platinum dish at 550 °C for 10 min. Weigh 100 g to 115 g sample in portions of 20 g to 40 g into the Pt dish, burn above a Bunsen burner, incinerate residues at 550 °C for 30 min in a muffle furnace, homogenize residue with soda-borax mix, melt over open flame, dissolve cooled melt cake in 6 ml HCl and 10 ml water, heat, and dilute to 50 ml for duplicate determinations.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12084 : 2018 is the national Indian Standard specification governing Morpholine, a critical cyclic organic chemical intermediate and volatile amine corrosion inhibitor extensively used in water-treatment for industrial boiler steam loops. Following the enforcement of the national chemical Quality Control Order (QCO), morpholine cannot be manufactured, imported, or sold in India without carrying the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Amendment No. 1 (August 2023) completely replaces the quality requirements of Table 1 and updates the standard to permit trace metal (Fe, Cu, Ni) and silica determinations through modern ICP-OES or ICP-MS instruments. It establishes strict sample-handling protocols in Annex F, detailing automated acid digestion at 320 °C and soda-borax platinum-dish fusions at 550 °C to eliminate organic remnants and ensure highly accurate, duplicate chemical analyses.
